title: Basic Science Facts
description: Foundational science knowledge: solar system, human body basics, animal classification, states of matter, and Earth science essentials. Grade tagged from 2 through 6.
subject: science
source: Next Generation Science Standards (NGSS) K-5 Earth/Space and Life Science performance expectations. Content reflects widely accepted elementary science curriculum.

items.prompt: What star is at the center of our solar system?
items.context: The Sun is a star, the closest one to Earth. The Moon goes around Earth, and Mars and Earth are planets that go around the Sun.

items.prompt: What planet do we live on?
What are the three states of matter we learn about first?
items.context: Most things around you are a solid (like a rock), a liquid (like milk), or a gas (like the air you breathe).

items.prompt: Which of these is an example of a LIQUID?
items.context: Water is a liquid: it flows and takes the shape of its cup. Ice is water frozen into a solid, and steam is water turned into a gas.

items.prompt: What do plants need to make food?
items.context: Plants use sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide from the air to make their own food. This is called photosynthesis.

items.prompt: Which animal lays eggs?
items.context: Chickens are birds, and all birds lay eggs. Dogs, cats, and cows are mammals, and their babies are born alive.

items.prompt: How many planets are in our solar system?
items.context: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006, leaving 8 official planets.

items.prompt: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
items.context: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun. Order from the Sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars.

items.prompt: Which is the largest planet in our solar system?
items.context: Jupiter is the biggest planet by far. More than 1,000 Earths could fit inside it. Saturn is second biggest.

items.prompt: What organ pumps blood through your body?
items.context: Your heart is a muscle about the size of your fist. It squeezes to push blood all around your body.

items.prompt: What organ do you breathe with?
items.context: Your lungs fill with air when you breathe in. They pass oxygen into your blood.

items.prompt: What is the process called when water turns into vapor?
items.context: Evaporation is when liquid water turns into a gas called water vapor, like a puddle drying up in the sun. Condensation is the opposite: vapor turning back into drops.

items.prompt: Which of these is a MAMMAL?
items.context: Dolphins look like fish but they are mammals. They breathe air and feed milk to their young.

items.prompt: What are the planets in order from the Sun?
items.answer: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune
choices: Venus, Mercury, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune
Mercury, Earth, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune
Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune
Mercury, Venus, Mars, Earth, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune
items.mnemonic: My Very Educated Mother Just Served Us Noodles.
items.context: Mercury is closest to the Sun and Neptune is farthest. Use the memory sentence: each word starts with a planet's first letter.

items.prompt: What is the main gas that makes up Earth's atmosphere?
items.context: Earth's atmosphere is about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen. We think of oxygen as the important one because we breathe it, but nitrogen is by far the most common.

items.prompt: Which is NOT a vertebrate (animal with a backbone)?
items.context: Octopuses are invertebrates (mollusks). Fish, frogs, and snakes all have backbones.

items.prompt: What is the largest organ in the human body?
items.context: Your skin covers your whole body, which makes it the largest organ. The liver is the largest organ inside your body.

items.prompt: What force pulls objects toward Earth?
items.context: Gravity is the pull that makes a dropped ball fall to the ground. It also keeps the Moon going around Earth.

items.prompt: What is the water cycle?
items.answer: Water rising into clouds and falling back as rain, over and over
choices: Water rising into clouds and falling back as rain, over and over
The Moon pulling ocean water into high and low tides each day
Water being cleaned at a plant and piped into our homes
Waves crashing on the beach and rolling back out to sea
items.context: The sun warms water so it evaporates into the air. The vapor cools into clouds (condensation), then falls as rain or snow (precipitation). Then it all starts again.

items.prompt: What are the three types of rocks?
items.context: Igneous rock forms when melted rock cools. Sedimentary rock forms from layers of sand and mud pressed together. Metamorphic rock is changed by heat and squeezing. (Granite, limestone, and marble are one of each.)

items.prompt: What do plant cells have that animal cells do NOT?
items.context: Plant cells have a stiff cell wall for support and chloroplasts that use sunlight to make food. Plant and animal cells both have a nucleus, cytoplasm, and a cell membrane.

items.prompt: What is the smallest living unit that all living things are made of?
items.context: Cells are the smallest living units: every plant, animal, and person is built from them. Atoms are much smaller, but an atom on its own isn't alive.

items.prompt: What do we call animals that eat only plants?
items.context: Herbivores eat only plants, like cows and rabbits. 'Herbi' comes from an old word for plants, like herbs. Carnivores eat meat.

items.prompt: What do we call animals that eat both plants and animals?
items.context: Humans are omnivores. Bears are omnivores. Pigs are omnivores.

items.prompt: When you breathe in, which gas from the air does your body use?
items.context: Your body uses oxygen to get energy from food. Air is mostly nitrogen, but you breathe it right back out without using it.

items.prompt: Which waste gas does your body make and then breathe out?
items.context: When your body uses oxygen, it makes carbon dioxide as waste, and you breathe it out. Plants take in that carbon dioxide to make their food.

items.prompt: What are the main layers of the Earth, from the outside in?
items.answer: Crust, mantle, outer core, inner core
choices: Crust, lava layer, rock layer, core
Crust, mantle, outer core, inner core
items.context: The crust is the thin rocky layer we live on. Below it is the mantle, hot rock that flows very slowly. The outer core is liquid metal and the inner core is solid metal.

items.prompt: What is the smallest piece of an element, like gold or iron, that is still that element?
items.context: Atoms are made of smaller particles (protons, neutrons, electrons) but atoms are the smallest unit that retains the properties of an element.

items.prompt: What process do plants use to make their own food?
items.context: 'Photo' means light and 'synthesis' means putting together: plants use light to make sugar from water and carbon dioxide. Respiration is how living things use food for energy.

items.prompt: What is the boiling point of water at sea level in Fahrenheit?
items.context: Water boils at 212 F or 100 C at sea level. At higher elevations it boils at lower temperatures.

items.prompt: What is the freezing point of water in Fahrenheit?
items.context: Water freezes at 32 degrees F, which is 0 degrees C. Zero degrees F is much colder than freezing.
